text:
support-jordan: FYI escalation — ACME reported SSO failures right after we onboarded their new tenant (acme-123). Assertion keeps getting routed to the org-level ACS rather than the tenant ACS. Customer hits 403 recipient mismatch and can't complete login.

infra-maria: Can you paste the SAMLResponse (redacted) and the request id? Also, any recent idp metadata refreshes or cert rotations?

support-jordan: Request-ID: req_0a9f3b2c. SAMLResponse (base64, redacted) shows Recipient: https://api.redwood.ai/sso/acs and NameID/Issuer look fine. RelayState includes tenant=acme-123. No cert rotation reported by the customer in last 72h. Quick repro we ran:
```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/sso/acs?RelayState=tenant%3Dacme-123" 
  -d "SAMLResponse=PHNhbWxSZXNwb25zZ....REDACTED...=="
```
Got 403 with message: "Recipient mismatch".

eng-lee: Two likely causes: 1) metadata merge produced a single canonical ACS list and the tenant entry got dropped/ordered last, or 2) our recipient validation is using the default org ACS when RelayState tenant binding is present but fails to look up tenant.bindings. Can you check the tenant->idp binding cache?

infra-maria: grep'd logs for req_0a9f3b2c — saw the lookup sequence: lookup idp by issuer -> load metadata from cache key idp_meta:acme-123 -> fallback to idp_meta:org-default. The cache hit was the org-default.

eng-lee: That suggests idp_meta:acme-123 is missing or stale. Run: `redis-cli GET idp_meta:acme-123`. If it's empty, our metadata-sync job probably failed to create per-tenant entry during onboarding.

support-jordan: Ran that, got null. But the onboarding flow returned success earlier. I pulled the onboarding audit: `POST /admin/tenants/acme-123/onboard` returned 200 and triggered metadata-sync job. Job logs show success, but target key write seems missing.

sre-olivia: Did anyone rotate IdP certs recently? If a rotation happened and metadata merge logic overwrote the per-tenant blob with org-default (matching cert thumbprint), that could explain ordering/override. Check metadata-sync service logs and the write calls.

support-jordan: No cert rotation reported by ACME. I grabbed the metadata-sync logs — near the onboarding time there's a WARN: "metadata merge produced duplicate keydescriptor; normalizing to canonical order" followed by an OK write to idp_meta:org-default but I don't see a write to idp_meta:acme-123.

eng-lee: I think we have a bug in the metadata-sync: when IdP has multiple EntityDescriptor/RoleDescriptor entries we were deduping and writing only the org-level key. Quick mitigation: in admin console we can add an "idp metadata override" for acme-123 with the tenant-specific ACS first. That will short-circuit cache lookup. Can someone add it and test?

support-jordan: I added a metadata override in the admin UI with tenant ACS first and forced a cache refresh. Test from customer still saw 403. Logs show we validated recipients against metadata override, but the request still used the org ACS because recipient check compares against `session.allowed_recipients` which is populated earlier from the base (org) metadata.

eng-lee: OK that's a validation-order bug. Two fixes: (A) make session.allowed_recipients prefer tenant override if present, (B) ensure metadata-sync writes per-tenant keys correctly. I'll open a patch to prefer tenant override at validation time as a hotfix.

infra-maria: Hotfix plan looks safe for a canary. We can patch service -> deploy to canary namespace for 10% traffic and run auth smoke tests. Eng, what's the PR ETA?

eng-lee: I'll have PR by EOD, tests in CI. Patch changes ~10 lines in recipient validation. If approved, canary deploy in ~2 hours. After canary, we'll schedule full rollout.

support-jordan: Noted. For customer messaging: told ACME we're investigating and suggested temporary workaround: have their IdP include tenant-specific ACS as first listed ACS in metadata. They said they can do that but prefer we fix on our side.

sre-olivia: Also add an incident tag and set priority to P2 (customer faced outage but partial workarounds). We should audit other tenants — run `redis-cli KEYS idp_meta:* | xargs -n1 redis-cli EXISTS` to find missing per-tenant keys.

support-jordan: Running that check now. Will DM results and update ticket.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: patch/recipient-tenant-override -> canary (10%) at 2024-04-01T14:30:00Z (deploy id: dpl_7b2f).

eng-lee: After canary, I also want to backfill missing idp_meta keys for tenants created in last 7 days — I'll add a migration job to re-run metadata-sync for any tenant missing a key.

support-jordan: Thanks all. Keeping ACME updated; will escalate to SME if canary shows issues.
